name: Super Indian
summary: Raj Comics' 2005 hero Aman, a clone of a terrorist chief raised by villains, then cleansed by a mystic to defend a future Indian city set in 2020.
origin: In the comics, Aman is a clone of the terrorist leader Ahankari, made by Dr Heathrow and trained by super-villains as a successor. Ahankari's father had the mystic Rudraksh Baba raise Aman instead and remove his inherited evil. Aman became Super Indian, wearing a dhoti and guarding Metro City.
powers: Skin turns blue when he senses evil

storyline.title: A clone is made
storyline.beat: After Ahankari nearly dies, Dr Heathrow makes a clone whose genes help him grow fast.

storyline.title: Raised by foes
storyline.beat: Super-villains train the clone to take over from Ahankari, so he learns all their weak spots.

storyline.title: Rudraksh Baba
storyline.beat: A mystic raises Aman to remove his inherited evil, and he takes the name Super Indian.

storyline.title: Uncle Metro
storyline.beat: He protects Metro City from the crime lord Uncle Metro, whose nephew Petro fell into a coma.

gossip.text: Raj Comics launched the series in its 20th year, setting it in a future Indian city in 2020.
The hero was raised by villains, so he knows their methods and they have nowhere to hide.
His skin turns blue when he senses evil, as a side effect of the darkness sealed in him.
He wears a dhoti, which the sources tie to his mystic training with Rudraksh Baba.

theme.tagline: Raised by villains, trained to save a city.

facts.text: Raj Comics announced SuperIndian in the publisher's 20th year, setting it in an ultra-modern Indian city in 2020, about fifteen years ahead of its readers.
The pitch was that he was raised by the era's biggest villains, who taught him everything, so he knows every one of their tricks and they have nowhere to hide.
Aman is a clone of the terrorist chief Ahankari, made after Ahankari had a near-fatal clash with an infiltrator named William Boother and wanted a successor.
Dr. Heathrow copied every aspect of Ahankari, and cloned genes sped up the clone's growth so he reached adulthood quickly.
Ahankari's own father feared the clone would inherit his son's malevolence and called in the mystic Rudraksh Baba to bring up his grandson.
In the story Rudraksh Baba purged the evil from the clone and confined it beneath a trident mark, which the comic links to Lord Shiva.
A strange side effect of that cleansing is that his skin turns blue whenever he senses evil.
He wears a traditional dhoti as a sign of his turn to mysticism, a very different costume from the usual spandex.
Because he has no relatives, he affectionately calls the members of P.O.E.M. (Protectors Of Earth & Mankind) his uncles and aunt.
Red Eyebrow, a scientific genius, lost the chance to build Metro City to another scientist and now wants to destroy the city and rebuild it himself.
Super Indian appears in Raj Comics' Kaal series, a crossover line that also features Ashwaraj, Gojo, Bhokal, TilismDev, Parmanu and Inspector Steel.
Raj Comics runs a Khoon series that is listed as a Doga and Super Indian pairing, so the hero raised by villains teams up with one of the publisher's grittiest heroes.
His titles include the playful Villain Chacha and Chemical Lochcha, a question-style Super Indian Kaun, and Project Setusamudram.
Raj Comics' first superhero was Nagraj, the snake hero; the idea came from Manoj Gupta in 1985 because snakes carry religious and mythological importance in India.
About 3.5 lakh copies of a single Nagraj title were printed at a time, according to ThePrint, a sign of how big Raj Comics got.
Over roughly 30 years Raj Comics published more than 3,500 titles, all of them in Hindi, which gave it a strong base in the Hindi belt but limited readers elsewhere.
In 1997 a TV advertisement for Nagraj starring Sonu Sood aired, and in the publisher's golden age it reportedly sold over a million copies a year.
Tarun Kumar Wahi, Super Indian's co-creator and Raj Comics' chief writer, also created Doga, Parmanu and Bheriya, so two of Super Indian's named allies, Doga and Bheriya, come from his own pen.
Raj Comics has made short films too: Aadamkhor in 2018, partly self-produced and crowdfunded on YouTube, and Doga - Mumbai Ka Rakhwala around 2019.
In 2015 Raj Comics released an Android app, which the publisher's page says earned a large following and an average rating above 4.5 stars.

kidSummary: Super Indian is a Raj Comics hero named Aman. He was made as a copy of a bad man and raised by villains, but a wise mystic cleansed him so he could protect people instead.

story.title: A copy is made
story.text: A terrorist leader named Ahankari has a scientist create a clone of himself, so he will have an heir.

story.title: Raised by villains
story.text: Super-villains teach the clone their tricks, so he learns exactly how they think.

story.title: A wise teacher
story.text: Ahankari's father worries and brings in the mystic Rudraksh Baba, who removes the evil from the clone.

story.title: A hero is born
story.text: The clone gets the name Aman and chooses to be Super Indian. His skin turns blue whenever he senses evil.

story.title: Guarding Metro City
story.text: He protects the high-tech Metro City and calls the heroes of P.O.E.M. his uncles and aunt.

timeline.title: SuperIndian announced
timeline.note: On 16 May 2005 Raj Comics announces a new series, SuperIndian, set in a futuristic Indian city in 2020, in the publisher's 20th year.

timeline.title: Launch planned for month-end
timeline.note: The announcement says the series is due by the end of that month, backed by a pre-launch buzz campaign and an online fan hub for posters and goodies.

timeline.title: Co-creator honoured
timeline.note: Tarun Kumar Wahi receives a Best Script Writer award from Raja Pocket Books CEO Manoj Gupta in 2010.

timeline.title: Raj Comics goes to Android
timeline.note: Super Indian's publisher releases an Android app for the general public in 2015.
